quranic_mention: Named 9 times; his people Thamud named 26 times
teaser: They asked for a sign, and Allah gave them a she-camel. They hamstrung it. Three days later a single cry ended a nation that carved its homes out of mountains.

layers.title: Who
layers.subtitle: Sent to Thamud — stone-cutters who carved palaces into cliffs at al-Hijr.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
«وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحًا» — "And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih." (Quran 7:73)

Thamud came after 'Ad and inherited the same warning without learning from it. Allah describes their achievement without mockery: «وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا» — "and you carve out of the mountains, homes." (Quran 7:74) And: «وَكَانُوا يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا آمِنِينَ» — "and they used to carve from the mountains, houses, feeling secure." (Quran 15:82)

That last word — آمِنِينَ, feeling secure — is the hinge of the whole story. They lived at al-Hijr in north-western Arabia, in stone dwellings that still stand today. Ibn Kathir notes they were given fertile land, springs, and date palms (Quran 26:147-148), and that Salih was from among their own noble lineage, respected before he was rejected.

layers.title: The Call
layers.subtitle: Worship Allah alone — and remember who gave you all of this.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
«يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُ» — the same opening as every prophet before him (Quran 7:73).

Then he grounded it in gratitude: «هُوَ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ وَاسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا» — "He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it." (Quran 11:61) Ibn Kathir explains this as: the same One who formed you from its soil is the One who gave you the ability to develop and inhabit it. Their engineering was itself a gift, not a self-generated right.

He listed the blessings by name — gardens, springs, crops, heavy-laden date palms — and then asked them to fear Allah and obey rather than «وَلَا تُطِيعُوا أَمْرَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ» — do not obey the command of the transgressors (Quran 26:151).

And he warned them with the specific arrogance of a comfortable nation: «أَتَتْرُكُونَ فِي مَا هُنَا آمِنِينَ» — do you think you will be left in what you have here, secure? (Quran 26:146)

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: The society split, and the ones who mattered socially were the ones who refused.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
The division was along status lines: «قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ أَتَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ صَالِحًا مُّرْسَلٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ» — the arrogant elite said to the oppressed believers: "Do you [really] know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" (Quran 7:75)

Before this, Salih had been trusted. They said: «قَدْ كُنتَ فِيْنَا مَرْجُوًّا قَبْلَ هَٰذَا» — "You were among us one in whom we had hope before this." (Quran 11:62) Ibn Kathir highlights this line: he lost his standing the moment he called them to tawhid. Respect that is conditional on silence was never respect.

Then a conspiracy formed. Surah an-Naml records nine men who plotted: «قَالُوا تَقَاسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ» — "they said: swear to one another by Allah that we will attack him and his family by night." (Quran 27:49) They swore by Allah's name to murder Allah's prophet.

layers.title: The Miracle
layers.subtitle: A she-camel with a share of the water — and the crime that ended a civilisation.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3378-3380 — the Prophet ﷺ at al-Hijr during the Tabuk expedition
layers.content:
They demanded a sign, and Allah answered: «هَٰذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً» — "This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you." (Quran 7:73) Its terms were simple and public: «لَهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُم شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ» — "For her is a [day of] drink, and for you a [day of] drink, [each] on a known day." (Quran 26:155) Do not harm her, and do not touch her share.

They killed her. «فَعَقَرُوهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا نَادِمِينَ» — "But they hamstrung her, and so became regretful." (Quran 26:157) Surah ash-Shams compresses the whole civilisation into one line: «فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا» — "and they denied him and hamstrung her." (Quran 91:14)

Allah gave them three days: «فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُوا فِي دَارِكُمْ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ» (Quran 11:65). Then: «فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّيْحَةُ» — the cry seized them (Quran 15:83), «فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ» — the earthquake seized them and morning found them lifeless in their homes (Quran 7:78). Their carved mountain fortresses became their tombs.

Centuries later the Prophet ﷺ passed al-Hijr on the way to Tabuk. He told his companions not to drink from its wells, covered his head, and urged his mount to move quickly, saying of such places: "Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, except while weeping, lest what befell them befall you." (Sahih al-Bukhari 3380-3381)

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: One man hamstrung the camel — and the whole nation was destroyed. The Quran explains why.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3377 — the man who hamstrung the she-camel was mighty and protected among his people
layers.content:
Surah al-Qamar names one actor: «فَنَادَىٰ صَاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ» — "But they called their companion, and he dared and hamstrung." (Quran 54:29) Yet Surah ash-Shams assigns the act to all of them: «فَعَقَرُوهَا» (Quran 91:14). Ibn Kathir resolves it exactly as the Quran does: one hand struck, and the nation consented. The Prophet ﷺ noted that the man who did it was mighty and well-protected within his tribe (Sahih al-Bukhari 3377) — he acted with the crowd behind him.

This is the enduring ruling of Thamud: silent approval is participation. A society is judged by what it permits.

Salih and the believers were saved: «نَجَّيْنَا صَالِحًا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنَّا» (Quran 11:66). And his last words to his people, after the camel was killed, are recorded as an indictment: «يَا قَوْمِ لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسَالَةَ رَبِّي وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُحِبُّونَ النَّاصِحِينَ» — "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors." (Quran 7:79)

Ibn Kathir's lesson is uncomfortable and permanent: the ruin of Thamud did not begin with hamstringing a camel. It began with a people who had come to dislike being advised.

quiz.prompt: What was Thamud known for, according to the Quran?

options.text: Seafaring and long-distance trade
Carving houses out of the mountains, feeling secure
Building pyramids of brick
Breeding horses for war

quiz.citation: Quran 15:82 — «وَكَانُوا يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا آمِنِينَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Quran records the skill and then the feeling that came with it — آمِنِينَ, secure. Their engineering was real; the safety they inferred from it was an illusion.

quiz.prompt: What were the terms attached to the she-camel Allah sent as a sign?

options.text: It was never to be looked at
It had its own day to drink, and they had theirs; it was not to be harmed
It had to be sacrificed each year
It was to be kept inside the city walls

quiz.citation: Quran 26:155 — «لَهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُم شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The test was small and entirely public: share the water. Allah's tests are rarely complicated; they are simply inconvenient.

quiz.prompt: How much time were Thamud given between hamstringing the camel and the punishment?

options.text: No time at all
Three days
Seven nights and eight days
Forty days

quiz.scholar_reflection: Even after the crime, a window for repentance was opened. Ibn Kathir notes they spent it waiting rather than turning back.

quiz.prompt: The Quran says one man hamstrung the camel, yet elsewhere attributes the act to the whole nation. What does this establish?

options.text: That the Quran contains a discrepancy
That the nation shared the guilt because it consented and protected him
That only that one man was punished
That the camel was killed twice

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ noted the man was mighty and shielded by his people. Silent approval made the act collective — the clearest Quranic statement that a society answers for what it permits.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct his companions when they passed al-Hijr, the ruins of Thamud, during the Tabuk expedition?

options.text: To camp there and rest
To take stones from it as souvenirs
Not to drink from its water, and to pass quickly and not enter such places except weeping
To rebuild the settlement

quiz.scholar_reflection: Sites of destroyed nations are not tourist attractions in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ treated them as places to be passed with fear, not curiosity.

quiz.prompt: Salih's people said, "You were one in whom we had hope before this" — they respected him until he called them to change. Have you felt that shift?

options.text: Yes — people liked me more before I took the deen seriously
Yes — at work, once I refused something everyone accepts
I have avoided it by keeping my convictions quiet
Not yet, and I am not sure whether that is peace or avoidance

quiz.citation: Quran 11:62 — «قَدْ كُنتَ فِيْنَا مَرْجُوًّا قَبْلَ هَٰذَا»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Approval that survives only while you stay silent was never approval of you. Salih lost his standing the day he stopped being convenient.
quiz.slider_label: How much of your standing depends on staying convenient?

quiz.prompt: Thamud carved homes in mountains and felt secure. Which structure in your life gives you that same feeling of being safe from disruption?

options.text: A stable job or income stream
A house, a city, a settled arrangement
A network of people who would catch me
My own competence — I can handle whatever comes

quiz.citation: Quran 15:82, Quran 26:146 — «أَتَتْرُكُونَ فِي مَا هُنَا آمِنِينَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Salih did not tell them to abandon their homes. He asked whether they believed the arrangement itself was permanent. Blessings become dangerous the moment they replace the Giver as the source of safety.
quiz.slider_label: If that structure vanished tomorrow, how much of your peace would go with it?

quiz.prompt: "You do not like advisors." How do you actually receive correction?

options.text: I defend myself first and consider it much later, if at all
I accept it from people I respect, and dismiss it from everyone else
I take it in silence but resent the person afterwards
I ask for it deliberately, and act on it

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Kathir places this line at the end of the story as its diagnosis. The camel was a symptom; the disease was a people who had stopped tolerating advice.
quiz.slider_label: How open are you to being corrected this week?

quiz.prompt: One man struck, and a nation consented by staying quiet. Where have you stayed silent about something you knew was wrong?

options.text: In my workplace, because objecting would cost me
In my family, to keep the peace
In a group of friends, because I did not want to be the difficult one
I do speak up, though not always at the right moment or in the right tone

quiz.citation: Quran 91:14 and Quran 54:29; cf. Sahih Muslim 49 on changing what is wrong
quiz.scholar_reflection: Thamud establishes that permission is participation. The Quran assigned one man's act to a whole people, and that ruling has never been repealed.
quiz.slider_label: How ready are you to say something the next time?

quiz.prompt: Allah gave them three days after the crime. What do you usually do with the gap between a wrong action and its consequence?

options.text: I wait and hope nothing comes of it
I busy myself so I do not have to think about it
I minimise it until it no longer feels like it needs repentance
I turn back quickly, before the feeling fades

quiz.scholar_reflection: Delay in punishment is itself a mercy and an opportunity. Thamud spent theirs waiting. The door of repentance stays open until it doesn't, and no one is shown the closing time.
quiz.slider_label: How fast do you usually turn back after a wrong?
